content.thinking:
I need to draft the postmortem with figure placeholders, starting with the symptom—account pages failing to load for many shoppers—and building the causal chain from there, beginning with the server error rate spike on account page requests.

The next why points to a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, triggered by the monthly-spend-feature flag being switched on; I'm tracing the flag evaluation data and confirming the revert restored service. I should double-check whether deploys or any earlier changes can be ruled out, since the records only show the one flag change before onset.

I'll avoid stating the exact line number and just reference the file or use the placeholder where needed. In plain terms: switching on the new monthly spending summary likely broke account pages because it divides by the number of purchases made this month, which is zero for shoppers who bought before but not this month — and since that faulty code still sits behind the flag, re-enabling monthly-spend-feature would probably cause the same failure again.

For contributing factors: first, the flag appears to have gone to all traffic at once rather than through a staged rollout, which is why a small division-by-zero bug became a full outage — a gradual rollout with automatic rollback could have caught it early. Second, there's no evidence of a test covering the flag-on path for shoppers without purchases that month, though new tests are being added as part of the fix. I'm also weighing whether the lack of paging counts as a true contributing factor or just a separate finding about alert routing.

For went_wrong, I'll note that no on-call page went out despite the alert firing. I'm drafting action items: staged rollout for flags, automatic revert tied to error-rate spikes, paging for this alert type, keeping the flag off until the fix is merged, and adding CI tests that run with each flag both on and off.

For went_well, I'm crediting Argus for reverting the flag and confirming recovery, and Code-Fix for quickly tracing the errors to the flag change and drafting a PR. I don't see strong candidates for got_lucky, so I'll likely leave that section empty.

For assumptions, I'm noting that the pre-incident ClientDisconnected errors were treated as unrelated baseline noise without being independently verified. For ruled-out causes, I'm confirming no deploys happened before onset, no rollout was in progress, and no other flag changes occurred in the hour before — all cited to their respective sources. I'm also pulling together the before/after evidence showing normal rendering while the flag was off and recovery after the revert, plus phrasing the symptom description around the share of failing requests without overstating specifics.

action_items.item: Require flags on io-shop, including monthly-spend-feature, to be turned on through a staged percentage rollout rather than for all traffic at once.
Automatically revert a flag change on io-shop when the account page error rate rises above its threshold soon after the change.
Run the io-shop account page tests with each feature flag both on and off in CI.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix proposed in PR #367, or an equivalent one, is deployed.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests failing with server errors rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That error first appeared at the onset and kept recurring while the service was broken.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: the production change events for the day before the onset returned no deploys, only the flag change.
A rollout still in progress: at {T10.1} all replicas were running one revision.
Another flag change: the flag provider showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before {T15.4}, the switch of monthly-spend-feature.

causal_chain.step: That code path ran because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations had been all off, and account pages rendered normally. In the onset minute evaluations were mixed between off and on, and after that they were all on. Reverting the flag at {T18.1} brought the service back below the incident's level from {T20.2}, and the action was judged confirmed.

With the flag on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`. That function divides the shopper's total for this month by the number of purchases they made this month. For a shopper with past purchases but none this month the list is empty, so the division at line {F1.1} raises ZeroDivisionError. This is the line the logged error points to.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly spending summary made account pages fail, most likely because the summary divides by the number of things a shopper bought this month, and for shoppers who bought before but not this month that number is zero.

contributing_factors.factor: No staged rollout or automatic guard was seen on the flag change. monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for all account page traffic within a minute.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Turning the flag on for a small share of traffic first, or reverting it automatically when errors rose, would have limited the failures to fewer shoppers or ended them sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that exercised the monthly summary path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix's tests for that case are new in its draft fix.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator tied the errors to the flag change by matching the ZeroDivisionError log lines and the flag evaluations to the change event, ranking that as its single candidate {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus reverted monthly-spend-feature {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed, {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the revert had brought the service back below the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened draft PR #367 {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, with new tests for the case it identified.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the HighErrorRate alert was not linked to any on-call incident.

input.root_cause: Switching on monthly-spend-feature makes `render_spend_summary` call `average_spend_per_item_this_month`. That function divides the shopper's total for this month by the number of purchases they made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty calculation was still in the code behind monthly-spend-feature, so switching that flag back on would most likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
